references.name: Alexis de Tocqueville
references.desc: Democracy in America — observed Americans' extraordinary propensity for civic association in the 1830s

references.name: Jane Jacobs
references.desc: The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961) — lauded neighborliness and street-level social capital

references.name: Mark Granovetter
references.desc: "The Strength of Weak Ties" — showed casual acquaintances are more valuable than close friends for jobs and information

references.name: Pierre Bourdieu
references.desc: French social theorist who formalized social capital as a resource embedded in networks

references.name: Glenn Loury
references.desc: Analyzed the social capital legacy of slavery and its impact on African American economic mobility

references.name: Ronald Burt
references.desc: Structural holes theory — executives with larger networks enjoy faster career advancement

references.name: Robert Wuthnow
references.desc: Leading scholar of the small-group movement; showed mainline churches encourage civic engagement while evangelicals focus inward

references.name: Diego Gambetta
references.desc: Scholar of trust and the Mafia; showed societies relying on force are less efficient than those maintained by trust

references.name: Mancur Olson
references.desc: The Logic of Collective Action — why rational individuals fail to act for group benefit (free-rider problem)

references.name: Christopher Bosso
references.desc: Expert on environmental fund-raising; showed direct mail turned members into "consumers of a cause"

references.name: Theda Skocpol
references.desc: Political scientist who documented the shift from mass-membership organizations to professional advocacy groups

references.name: Alan Wolfe
references.desc: Interviewed middle-class suburbanites; found work had replaced neighborhoods as primary source of community

references.name: Kenneth Wald
references.desc: "Religious ideals are potentially powerful sources of commitment" — studied faith as civic motivator
